valid_fixes: Remove ReservedConcurrentExecutions from CSVProcessingToSQSFunction.Properties and fix the s3:GetObject Resource ARN suffix from raw-uploads/* to inventory-updates/* — both changes are required
invalid_patches: Fixing only ReservedConcurrentExecutions without correcting the s3:GetObject resource — parser runs but fails with AccessDenied on every GetObject call
Fixing only the s3:GetObject resource without removing ReservedConcurrentExecutions: 0 — parser remains permanently throttled and never invoked
optimal_diagnostic_path: ace_check_queue_depth(queue=InventoryUpdatesQueue) → visible=0, in_flight=0 — no messages ever arrived
ace_get_log_tail(function=CSVProcessingToSQSFunction) → AccessDenied: s3:GetObject on ace-bench-stack-inventory-updates bucket (after concurrency fix)
ace_get_iam_role(role=InventoryFunctionRole) → s3:GetObject Resource ends in raw-uploads/* instead of inventory-updates/*; ace_simulate_policy confirms implicitDeny
observable_symptom: CSV upload succeeds. Queue depth stays at zero. Consumer is never invoked. The CSV parser produces zero log output — not even a function start entry — because throttled invocations are rejected before initialization. No error surfaces without inspecting the parser's concurrency configuration.
root_cause: CSVProcessingToSQSFunction has ReservedConcurrentExecutions set to 0, which throttles all invocations before execution begins and produces no logs. After removing the concurrency limit, the parser is invoked but immediately fails with AccessDenied on s3:GetObject because the IAM role's s3:GetObject Resource ARN references raw-uploads/* instead of inventory-updates/*. Both faults must be corrected for the pipeline to function.
